articles.title: 完型 · 智力差异、遗传疾病与自然选择
articles.context: 科学争议与进化解释。前半先制造“禁忌假说”的张力，后半把高智力表现与遗传疾病并置并提出自然选择解释；保持理性、克制，转折和因果链清楚。
rows: The idea that some groups of people may be more intelligent than others is one of those hypotheses that dare not speak its name.
某些群体可能比另一些群体更聪明，这种假说属于人们讳莫如深、不敢公开谈论的话题。
But Gregory Cochran is prepared to say it anyway.
但格雷戈里·科克伦还是准备把它说出来。
He is that rare bird, a scientist who works independently of any institution.
他属于少见的那一类科学家：不依附于任何机构，独立开展研究。
He helped popularize the idea that some diseases not previously thought to have a bacterial cause were actually infections, which aroused much controversy when it was first suggested.
他曾推动一种观点广为人知：一些过去并不认为由细菌引起的疾病，其实属于感染性疾病；这一观点刚提出时曾引发很大争议。
Even he, however, might tremble at the thought of what he is about to do.
然而，即便是他，想到自己接下来要做的事，也可能会心里发怵。

Together with another two scientists, he is publishing a paper which not only suggests that one group of humanity is more intelligent than the others, but explains the process that has brought this about.
他正与另外两位科学家共同发表一篇论文；论文不仅提出某一人类群体比其他群体更聪明，还试图解释这种差异形成的过程。
The group in question are a particular people originated from central Europe.
这里所说的群体，是一个源自中欧的特定族群。
而这个过程，就是自然选择。

This group generally do well in IQ tests, scoring 12-15 points above the mean value of 100, and have contributed disproportionately to the intellectual and cultural life of the West, as the careers of their elites, including several world-renowned scientists, affirm.
这一群体通常在智商测试中表现出色，得分比100分的平均值高出12至15分；而且他们对西方思想与文化生活的贡献远超其人口比例，这一点从其精英人物——包括多位世界知名科学家——的成就中即可得到印证。
They also suffer more often than most people from a number of nasty genetic diseases, such as breast cancer.
与此同时，他们罹患某些严重遗传性疾病——例如乳腺癌——的频率也高于大多数人。
These facts, however, have previously been thought unrelated.
然而，过去人们一直认为这两类事实彼此无关。
The former has been put down to social effects, such as a strong tradition of valuing education.
前一种现象通常被归因于社会因素，例如重视教育的深厚传统。
The latter was seen as a consequence of genetic isolation.
后一种现象则被视为遗传隔离的结果。
Dr. Cochran suggests that the intelligence and diseases are intimately linked.
科克伦博士则认为，这种智力表现与这些疾病之间存在密切联系。
His argument is that the unusual history of these people has subjected them to unique evolutionary pressures that have resulted in this paradoxical state of affairs.
他的论点是：这个族群不同寻常的历史使其承受了独特的进化压力，最终形成了这种看似矛盾的局面。

articles.title: 阅读一 · 女性为何更易受到长期压力影响
articles.context: 性别差异与压力反应。文章先从生理反应解释女性对压力的易感性，再转向女性承担更多、更加长期和重复的人际压力，最后以单亲母亲经历落到现实生活。语气理性、同理但不过度煽情，因果与对比处清晰。
rows: While still catching up to men in some spheres of modern life, women appear to be way ahead in at least one undesirable category.
尽管在现代生活的一些领域女性仍在追赶男性，但至少在一个并不令人羡慕的方面，女性似乎远远走在了前面。

‘Women are particularly susceptible to developing depression and anxiety disorders in response to stress compared to men,’ according to Dr. Yehuda, chief psychiatrist at New York's Veterans Administration Hospital.
纽约退伍军人管理局医院精神科主任耶胡达博士指出：“与男性相比，女性在面对压力时尤其容易出现抑郁和焦虑障碍。”

Studies of both animals and humans have shown that sex hormones somehow affect the stress response, causing females under stress to produce more of the trigger chemicals than do males under the same conditions.
对动物和人类的研究都表明，性激素会以某种方式影响压力反应，使处于压力中的雌性个体比相同条件下的雄性产生更多触发压力反应的化学物质。
In several of the studies, when stressed-out female rats had their ovaries removed, their chemical responses became equal to those of the males.
在其中几项研究中，当处于压力状态的雌鼠被摘除卵巢后，它们的化学反应就变得与雄鼠相同。
equal to those of the males
Adding to a woman's increased dose of stress chemicals are her increased ‘opportunities’ for stress.
除了体内会产生更多压力相关化学物质之外，女性遭遇压力的“机会”也更多。
‘It's not necessarily that women don't cope as well.
“并不一定是女性更不善于应对压力。
It's just that they have so much more to cope with,’ says Dr. Yehuda.
问题只是，她们需要应付的事情实在多得多。”耶胡达博士说。
so much more to cope with

‘Their capacity for tolerating stress may even be greater than men's,’ she observes, ‘it's just that they're dealing with so many more things that they become worn out from it more visibly and sooner.’
她指出：“女性承受压力的能力甚至可能比男性更强，只是她们同时要处理的事情太多，所以压力带来的疲惫会更早、更明显地表现出来。”
Dr. Yehuda notes another difference between the sexes.
耶胡达博士还指出了男女之间的另一个差异。
‘I think that the kinds of things that women are exposed to tend to be in more of a chronic or repeated nature.
“我认为，女性所面对的事情往往更具有长期性或反复性。
Men go to war and are exposed to combat stress.
男性会上战场，承受战争带来的压力。
Men are exposed to more acts of random physical violence.
男性也更多地遭遇随机性的身体暴力。
The kinds of interpersonal violence that women are exposed to tend to be in domestic situations, by, unfortunately, parents or other family members, and they tend not to be one-shot deals.
而女性所遭遇的人际暴力往往发生在家庭环境中，施暴者不幸地常常是父母或其他家庭成员，而且这种暴力通常不是一次性的。
The wear-and-tear that comes from these longer relationships can be quite devastating.’
这些长期关系造成的持续消耗可能具有相当大的破坏性。”
Adeline Alvarez married at 18 and gave birth to a son, but was determined to finish college.
阿德琳·阿尔瓦雷斯18岁结婚并生下一个儿子，但她仍决心完成大学学业。
‘I struggled a lot to get the college degree.
“为了拿到大学学位，我付出了很多艰辛。
I was living in so much frustration that that was my escape, to go to school, and get ahead and do better.’
那时我的生活充满挫折，去上学成了我的一种逃离方式，我想借此向前走，让生活变得更好。”
Later, her marriage ended and she became a single mother.
后来，她的婚姻结束了，她成了一名单亲母亲。
‘It's the hardest thing to take care of a teenager, have a job, pay the rent, pay the car payment, and pay the debt.
“一边照顾青春期的孩子，一边工作，还要付房租、车贷和债务，这实在是最艰难的事情。
I lived from paycheck to paycheck.’
我的日子就是靠一张工资支票接着一张工资支票勉强维持。”
Not everyone experiences the kinds of severe chronic stresses Alvarez describes.
并不是每个人都会经历阿尔瓦雷斯所描述的那种严重而长期的压力。
But most women today are coping with a lot of obligations, with few breaks, and feeling the strain.
但如今大多数女性都要承担许多责任，几乎没有喘息的机会，并因此感受到压力。
Alvarez's experience demonstrates the importance of finding ways to diffuse stress before it threatens your health and your ability to function.
阿尔瓦雷斯的经历说明，在压力威胁到健康和正常生活能力之前，找到缓解压力的方法十分重要。

articles.title: 阅读二 · 科学出版从订阅制走向开放获取
articles.context: 科学传播与出版制度变化。先回顾传统同行评议和订阅模式，再解释互联网、资助机构压力与开放获取商业模式如何改变科学成果传播。语气理性、清楚，制度变化和三种新模式处加强信息重音。
rows: It used to be so straightforward.
过去，这件事的流程一直非常简单直接。
A team of researchers working together in the laboratory would submit the results of their research to a journal.
一组在实验室共同工作的研究人员会把研究结果投稿给一家学术期刊。
A journal editor would then remove the authors' names and affiliations from the paper and send it to their peers for review.
随后，期刊编辑会从论文中删去作者姓名和所属机构，再把论文送交同行评审。
Depending on the comments received, the editor would accept the paper for publication or decline it.
编辑会根据收到的评审意见决定接受论文发表，或予以拒绝。
Copyright rested with the journal publisher, and researchers seeking knowledge of the results would have to subscribe to the journal.
论文版权归期刊出版商所有，而想了解研究结果的研究人员则必须订阅该期刊。
如今，情况已经不再如此。

The Internet—and pressure from funding agencies, who are questioning why commercial publishers are making money from government-funded research by restricting access to it—is making access to scientific results a reality.
互联网的发展，加上资助机构施加的压力，正在使科研成果真正变得可获取；这些资助机构质疑，商业出版商为何能够通过限制访问由政府资助的研究来牟利。
The Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) has just issued a report describing the far-reaching consequences of this.
经济合作与发展组织（OECD）刚刚发布了一份报告，说明这一变化将带来的深远影响。
The report, by John Houghton of Victoria University in Australia and Graham Vickery of the OECD, makes heavy reading for publishers who have, so far, made handsome profits.
这份由澳大利亚维多利亚大学的约翰·霍顿和 OECD 的格雷厄姆·维克里撰写的报告，对那些迄今利润丰厚的出版商来说并不好受。
But it goes further than that.
但它所涉及的意义远不止于此。
It signals a change in what has, until now, been a key element of scientific endeavor.
它预示着科学事业中一个长期以来的关键环节正在发生变化。
The value of knowledge and the return on the public investment in research depends, in part, upon wide distribution and ready access.
知识的价值以及公共科研投入所获得的回报，在一定程度上取决于科研成果能否被广泛传播并方便获取。
这同时也是一门大生意。
In America, the core scientific publishing market is estimated at between $7 billion and $11 billion.
据估计，美国核心科学出版市场的规模在70亿至110亿美元之间。
The International Association of Scientific, Technical and Medical Publishers says that there are more than 2,000 publishers worldwide specializing in these subjects.
国际科学、技术与医学出版商协会称，全球有两千多家出版机构专门从事这些领域的出版。
They publish more than 1.2 million articles each year in some 16,000 journals.
这些出版机构每年在大约1.6万种期刊上发表超过120万篇文章。
而现在，这一格局正在改变。
According to the OECD report, some 75% of scholarly journals are now online.
根据 OECD 的报告，目前大约75%的学术期刊已经上线。
Entirely new business models are emerging; three main ones were identified by the report's authors.
全新的商业模式正在出现；报告作者归纳出了其中三种主要模式。
There is the so-called big deal, where institutional subscribers pay for access to a collection of online journal titles through site-licensing agreements.
第一种是所谓的“大宗协议”：机构订阅者通过网站许可协议付费，获得一批在线期刊的访问权。
There is open-access publishing, typically supported by asking the author (or his employer) to pay for the paper to be published.
第二种是开放获取出版，通常由作者或其雇主支付论文发表费用来维持。
Finally, there are open-access archives, where organizations such as universities or international laboratories support institutional repositories.
最后一种是开放获取档案库，由大学或国际实验室等机构支持建设机构知识库。

Other models exist that are hybrids of these three, such as delayed open-access, where journals allow only subscribers to read a paper for the first six months, before making it freely available to everyone who wishes to see it.
此外还存在这三种模式的混合形式，例如延迟开放获取：论文发表后的前六个月只允许订阅者阅读，之后再向所有希望阅读的人免费开放。
All this could change the traditional form of the peer-review process, at least for the publication of papers.
所有这些变化都可能改变传统同行评议流程的形式，至少会改变论文发表这一环节。

articles.title: 阅读三 · 美国人的身高已接近遗传上限
articles.context: 人体生长与遗传限制。文章先用 NBA 球员变高制造表面印象，再区分职业体育招募效应与普通美国人身高停滞，最后解释营养改善和遗传约束。语气科学、清晰，统计数据与反直觉结论处加强重音。
rows: In the early 1960s Wilt Chamberlain was one of the only three players in the National Basketball Association (NBA) listed at over seven feet.
20世纪60年代初，威尔特·张伯伦是美国职业篮球联赛（NBA）中仅有的三名身高超过7英尺的球员之一。
If he had played last season, however, he would have been one of 42.
然而，如果他参加的是上一个赛季，他就只会是42名这类球员中的一员。

The bodies playing major professional sports have changed dramatically over the years, and managers have been more than willing to adjust team uniforms to fit the growing numbers of bigger, longer frames.
多年来，参加主要职业体育赛事的运动员体型发生了显著变化，管理者也非常愿意调整队服，以适应越来越多更高大、更修长的体型。
The trend in sports, though, may be obscuring an unrecognized reality: Americans have generally stopped growing.
不过，体育界的这一趋势可能掩盖了一个尚未被充分认识的事实：美国人的身高总体上已经停止增长。

Though typically about two inches taller now than 140 years ago, today's people—especially those born to families who have lived in the U.S. for many generations—apparently reached their limit in the early 1960s.
尽管今天的人通常比140年前高约2英寸，但如今的人——尤其是那些家族已在美国生活多代的人——显然在20世纪60年代初就已接近身高极限。
And they aren't likely to get any taller.
而且他们今后也不太可能再变得更高。
aren't likely to get any taller
‘In the general population today, at this genetic, environmental level, we've pretty much gone as far as we can go,’ says anthropologist William Cameron Chumlea of Wright State University.
莱特州立大学人类学家威廉·卡梅伦·丘姆利亚说：“就今天普通人群所处的遗传和环境水平而言，我们基本已经走到极限了。”
as far as we can go
In the case of NBA players, their increase in height appears to result from the increasingly common practice of recruiting players from all over the world.
至于 NBA 球员，他们身高上升似乎源于一种越来越普遍的做法：从世界各地招募球员。
recruiting players from all over the world
Growth, which rarely continues beyond the age of 20, demands calories and nutrients—notably, protein—to feed expanding tissues.
人体生长很少会持续到20岁以后，而生长需要热量和营养物质——尤其是蛋白质——来供给不断扩张的组织。
At the start of the 20th century, under-nutrition and childhood infections got in the way.
20世纪初，营养不足和儿童期感染阻碍了身体生长。
But as diet and health improved, children and adolescents have, on average, increased in height by about an inch and a half every 20 years, a pattern known as the secular trend in height.
但随着饮食和健康状况改善，儿童和青少年的平均身高每20年约增加1.5英寸，这一规律被称为身高的长期趋势。
an inch and a half every 20 years
Yet according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, average height—5'9" for men, 5'4" for women—hasn't really changed since 1960.
然而，根据美国疾病控制与预防中心的数据，男性平均身高5英尺9英寸、女性5英尺4英寸，这一水平自1960年以来其实并没有真正变化。
Genetically speaking, there are advantages to avoiding substantial height.
从遗传角度看，避免过高的身材其实具有一定优势。
During childbirth, larger babies have more difficulty passing through the birth canal.
分娩时，体型较大的婴儿更难通过产道。

Moreover, even though humans have been upright for millions of years, our feet and back continue to struggle with bipedal posture and cannot easily withstand repeated strain imposed by oversize limbs.
此外，尽管人类已经直立行走了数百万年，我们的双脚和背部仍在承受双足姿势带来的负担，也难以轻松承受过长肢体所造成的反复压力。
‘There are some real constraints that are set by the genetic architecture of the individual organism,’ says anthropologist William Leonard of Northwestern University.
西北大学人类学家威廉·伦纳德说：“个体自身的遗传结构确实设定了一些实际限制。”
Genetic maximums can change, but don't expect this to happen soon.
遗传意义上的最大值可以改变，但不要指望这种变化很快发生。
don't expect this to happen soon
Claire C. Gordon, senior anthropologist at the Army Research Center in Natick, Mass., ensures that 90 percent of the uniforms and workstations fit recruits without alteration.
马萨诸塞州纳蒂克陆军研究中心的高级人类学家克莱尔·C·戈登负责确保90%的制服和工作台无需改动就能适合新兵。
She says that, unlike those for basketball, the length of military uniforms has not changed for some time.
她说，与篮球服不同，军服的长度已经有一段时间没有变化了。
And if you need to predict human height in the near future to design a piece of equipment, Gordon says that by and large, ‘you could use today's data and feel fairly confident.’
戈登表示，如果为了设计设备而需要预测不久将来的人体身高，那么总体而言，“采用今天的数据就可以相当有把握”。

articles.title: 阅读四 · 美国建国者与奴隶制的道德妥协
articles.context: 美国建国史与奴隶制。文章从华盛顿鲜为人知的牙齿移植细节切入，转向历史学界对建国者、奴隶制与政治妥协的重新审视。保持克制、历史叙述感，在道德矛盾、制度利益和人物转变处加强重音。
rows: In 1784, five years before he became president of the United States, George Washington, 52, was nearly toothless.
1784年，也就是出任美国总统前五年，52岁的乔治·华盛顿几乎已经没有牙齿。
So he hired a dentist to transplant nine teeth into his jaw—having extracted them from the mouths of his slaves.
于是，他雇了一名牙医，把九颗牙齿移植到自己的下颌中——这些牙齿是从他的奴隶口中拔下来的。
from the mouths of his slaves
That's a far different image from the cherry-tree-chopping George most people remember from their history books.
这与大多数人从历史课本中记得的那个“砍樱桃树的乔治”形象大不相同。
But recently, many historians have begun to focus on the roles slavery played in the lives of the founding generation.
但近年来，许多历史学家开始关注奴隶制在美国建国一代人的生活中所扮演的角色。
focus on the roles slavery played
They have been spurred in part by DNA evidence made available in 1998, which almost certainly proved Thomas Jefferson had fathered at least one child with his slave Sally Hemings.
促使他们转向这一问题的原因之一，是1998年出现的 DNA 证据；这些证据几乎可以确定，托马斯·杰斐逊至少与其奴隶萨莉·海明斯生过一个孩子。
And only over the past 30 years have scholars examined history from the bottom up.
而且，学者们也只是在过去30年里才开始从底层视角重新审视历史。
Works of several historians reveal the moral compromises made by the nation's early leaders and the fragile nature of the country's infancy.
几位历史学家的著作揭示了美国早期领导人所作的道德妥协，以及这个国家初创时期的脆弱处境。
More significantly, they argue that many of the Founding Fathers knew slavery was wrong—and yet most did little to fight it.
更重要的是，他们认为，许多建国先贤明知奴隶制是错误的，却几乎没有真正采取行动去反对它。
More than anything, the historians say, the founders were hampered by the culture of their time.
历史学家认为，最重要的是，建国者受到了他们所处时代文化的束缚。
hampered by the culture of their time
While Washington and Jefferson privately expressed distaste for slavery, they also understood that it was part of the political and economic bedrock of the country they helped to create.
虽然华盛顿和杰斐逊私下都表达过对奴隶制的反感，但他们也明白，奴隶制是他们参与建立的这个国家政治和经济基础的一部分。
For one thing, the South could not afford to part with its slaves.
首先，南方在经济上承受不起失去奴隶的代价。
could not afford to part with
Owning slaves was ‘like having a large bank account,’ says Wiencek, author of An Imperfect God: George Washington, His Slaves, and the Creation of America.
《不完美的上帝：乔治·华盛顿、他的奴隶与美国的创立》一书作者温塞克说，拥有奴隶“就像拥有一个大额银行账户”。
like having a large bank account

The southern states would not have signed the Constitution without protections for the ‘peculiar institution,’ including a clause that counted a slave as three fifths of a man for purposes of congressional representation.
如果宪法没有为这种“特殊制度”提供保护，南方各州就不会签署宪法；其中一项条款甚至规定，在计算国会代表名额时，一名奴隶按五分之三个人计算。
And the statesmen's political lives depended on slavery.
而这些政治家的政治生涯同样依赖于奴隶制。
The three-fifths formula handed Jefferson his narrow victory in the presidential election of 1800 by inflating the votes of the southern states in the Electoral College.
三分之五折算公式提高了南方各州在选举人团中的票数，从而帮助杰斐逊在1800年总统选举中险胜。
Once in office, Jefferson extended slavery with the Louisiana Purchase in 1803; the new land was carved into 13 states, including three slave states.
杰斐逊上台后又通过1803年的路易斯安那购地扩大了奴隶制；这片新领土后来被划分为13个州，其中有3个蓄奴州。
Still, Jefferson freed Hemings's children—though not Hemings herself or his approximately 150 other slaves.
尽管如此，杰斐逊还是释放了海明斯的孩子们——但并没有释放海明斯本人，也没有释放自己其余大约150名奴隶。

Washington, who had begun to believe that all men were created equal after observing the bravery of the black soldiers during the Revolutionary War, overcame the strong opposition of his relatives to grant his slaves their freedom in his will.
华盛顿在独立战争期间目睹黑人士兵的英勇表现后，开始相信人人生而平等；后来他克服亲属的强烈反对，在遗嘱中给予自己的奴隶自由。
Only a decade earlier, such an act would have required legislative approval in Virginia.
而仅仅在十年前，这样的举动在弗吉尼亚还必须得到立法机关批准。

articles.title: 新题型 · 如何完成论文初稿并反复修改
articles.context: 写作方法指导。按原题正确匹配 D-G-A-C-E 还原完整文章，只保留真正属于正文的五个插入段，排除两个干扰项、题号与 Directions。语气实用、直接，像有经验的写作者面对面指导。
rows: The time for sharpening pencils, arranging your desk, and doing almost anything else instead of writing has ended.
削铅笔、整理书桌，以及做几乎所有事情来逃避写作的时间已经结束了。
The first draft will appear on the page only if you stop avoiding the inevitable and sit, stand up, or lie down to write.
只有当你不再逃避这件不可避免的事，真正坐下、站着或躺下来开始写，初稿才会出现在纸面上。
It makes no difference how you write, just so you do.
你采用什么姿势、什么方式写并不重要，重要的是你真的开始写。
Now that you have developed a topic into a tentative thesis, you can assemble your notes and begin to flesh out whatever outline you have made.
既然你已经把一个主题发展成暂定的论点，就可以整理笔记，并开始充实已经拟好的提纲。
Your outline should smoothly conduct you from one point to the next, but do not permit it to railroad you.
提纲应当顺畅地引导你从一个要点走向下一个，但不要让它反过来束缚你。
do not permit it to railroad you
If a relevant and important idea occurs to you now, work it into the draft.
如果此时想到一个相关而重要的观点，就把它写进初稿。
By using the first draft as a means of thinking about what you want to say, you will very likely discover more than your notes originally suggested.
把初稿当作思考自己究竟想表达什么的工具，你很可能会发现比原有笔记更多的内容。
Plenty of good writers don't use outlines at all but discover ordering principles as they write.
许多优秀作家根本不使用提纲，而是在写作过程中逐渐发现材料的组织原则。
Do not attempt to compose a perfectly correct draft the first time around.
不要试图第一次就写出一份完全正确的初稿。
Grammar, punctuation, and spelling can wait until you revise.
语法、标点和拼写都可以等到修改阶段再处理。
Concentrate on what you are saying.
先集中精力想清楚自己在说什么。
Good writing most often occurs when you are in hot pursuit of an idea rather than in a nervous search for errors.
好文章往往产生于你全力追逐一个观点的时候，而不是产生于紧张地四处搜寻错误的时候。
To make revising easier, leave wide margins and extra space between lines so that you can easily add words, sentences, and corrections.
为了便于修改，要留出较宽的页边距和较大的行间距，这样就能方便地添加词语、句子和修改内容。
Write on only one side of the paper.
Your pages will be easier to keep track of that way, and, if you have to clip a paragraph to place it elsewhere, you will not lose any writing on the other side.
这样更容易整理各页；如果需要剪下一段放到别处，也不会因此丢掉纸张背面的文字。
If you are working on a word processor, you can take advantage of its capacity to make additions and deletions as well as move entire paragraphs by making just a few simple keyboard commands.
如果使用文字处理软件，你可以利用它增删内容的功能，也可以只用几个简单的键盘命令移动整段文字。
Some software programs can also check spelling and certain grammatical elements in your writing.
有些软件程序还可以检查拼写以及文章中的某些语法问题。
It's worth remembering, however, that though a clean copy fresh off a printer may look terrific, it will read only as well as the thinking and writing that have gone into it.
不过值得记住的是，一份刚从打印机出来的整洁稿件看起来也许很漂亮，但它读起来究竟有多好，最终仍取决于其中投入的思考和写作质量。
Many writers prudently store their data on disks and print their pages each time they finish a draft to avoid losing any material because of power failures or other problems.
许多写作者会谨慎地把资料存入磁盘，并在每完成一稿后把页面打印出来，以避免因停电或其他问题丢失材料。
These printouts are also easier to read than the screen when you work on revisions.
在修改时，这些打印稿也比屏幕上的文字更容易阅读。
easier to read than the screen
Once you have a first draft on paper, you can delete material that is unrelated to your thesis and add material necessary to illustrate your points and make your paper convincing.
一旦初稿已经落在纸面上，你就可以删去与论点无关的材料，并补入说明观点、增强文章说服力所必需的内容。
The student who wrote ‘The A&P as a State of Mind’ wisely dropped a paragraph that questioned whether Sammy displays chauvinistic attitudes toward women.
写《A&P 作为一种心态》的那名学生明智地删掉了一段讨论萨米是否对女性表现出大男子主义态度的文字。
Although this is an interesting issue, it has nothing to do with the thesis, which explains how the setting influences Sammy's decision to quit his job.
尽管这是个有意思的问题，却与文章论点无关；这篇文章要说明的是环境如何影响萨米辞职的决定。
nothing to do with the thesis
Instead of including that paragraph, she added one that described Lengel's crabbed response to the girls so that she could lead up to the A&P ‘policy’ he enforces.
她没有保留那一段，而是加入了一段描写伦格尔如何不耐烦地回应那些女孩的文字，从而自然引出他所执行的 A&P 商店“规定”。
Remember that your initial draft is only that.
要记住，你的初稿就只是初稿而已。
You should go through the paper many times—and then again—working to substantiate and clarify your ideas.
你应该把文章反复检查许多遍，甚至再来一遍，不断充实并澄清自己的观点。
You may even end up with several entire versions of the paper.
最后你甚至可能得到好几个完整版本。
The sentences within each paragraph should be related to a single topic.
每一段中的句子都应围绕同一个主题。
Transitions should connect one paragraph to the next so that there are no abrupt or confusing shifts.
段落之间应通过过渡衔接起来，避免出现突兀或令人困惑的跳转。
Awkward or wordy phrasing or unclear sentences and paragraphs should be mercilessly poked and prodded into shape.
对于别扭、啰嗦的表达，以及含混不清的句子和段落，都应毫不留情地反复推敲、修改成形。

articles.title: 翻译 · 达尔文对自身智力与审美变化的反思
articles.context: 达尔文晚年对自身认知能力、推理能力与审美变化的克制反思。只保留46-50五个划线目标句。
rows: He believes that this very difficulty may have had the compensating advantage of forcing him to think long and intently about every sentence, and thus enabling him to detect errors in reasoning and in his own observations.
他认为，正是这种表达上的困难也许反而带来了一种补偿性的好处：它迫使自己长时间、专注地推敲每一个句子，从而使他能够发现推理中的错误以及自己观察中的偏差。
He asserted, also, that his power to follow a long and purely abstract train of thought was very limited, for which reason he felt certain that he never could have succeeded with mathematics.
他还声称，自己沿着一条漫长而纯粹抽象的思路持续思考的能力十分有限，因此他确信自己绝不可能在数学上取得成功。
On the other hand, he did not accept as well founded the charge made by some of his critics that, while he was a good observer, he had no power of reasoning.
另一方面，对于一些批评者提出的指责——认为他虽然善于观察，却没有推理能力——他并不认为这种说法有充分根据。
did not accept as well founded
He adds humbly that perhaps he was ‘superior to the common run of men in noticing things which easily escape attention, and in observing them carefully.’
他谦逊地补充说，也许自己只是“比普通人更善于注意那些容易被忽略的事物，并对它们进行细致观察”。
superior to the common run of men
Darwin was convinced that the loss of these tastes was not only a loss of happiness, but might possibly be injurious to the intellect, and more probably to the moral character.
达尔文确信，失去这些审美趣味不仅意味着失去快乐，而且还可能有损智力，更可能有损道德品格。
not only a loss of happiness
